messages:
acme_infra: Hey support — our integration with structured_json mode started failing this morning. We get a parse error when the API returns a JSON array of items. Example response: `Invalid JSON: unexpected token at position 124`.
sarah_support: Sorry to hear that, can you paste the request payload (sanitized) and an exact snippet of the API response you got? Also which model + client SDK version?

acme_infra: Request (node fetch):
```js
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer xxxxx', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    model: 'redwood-13b-v1',
    mode: 'structured_json',
    json_schema: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', required: ['id','title'], properties: { id: {type:'string'}, title:{type:'string'}, meta:{type:'object'} } } },
    prompt: 'List 2 results as JSON array with fields id, title, meta',
    stream: true
  })
})
```

And here's the received stream chunk (we concatenated chunks):
```
[{"id":"r1","title":"First result","meta":{"score":0.9}},{"id":"r2","title":
"Second result","meta":{"score":0.8,"extra":"x"}},{"id":"r3","titl","meta":{}}]
```
This obviously breaks the parser (partial object for r3 and an extra key on r2). Happening regularly at peak QPS.

mike_eng: Thanks — couple quick q's: 1) Are you seeing this only with streaming on? 2) Is ordering of items important to you (are you assuming stable array order)? 3) Do you have request ids to share (X-Request-ID header) so we can look up logs?

acme_infra: 1) yes mostly when stream:true. 2) we do rely on order (ranked results). 3) example request id: req_20260310_9ab3fd (added in header).

sarah_support: Opening an escalation to eng-runtime and eng-ml. Tagging: @mike_eng @julia_ml. Ticket #SUP-4821.
support-bot: Created ticket SUP-4821 and attached initial request payload.

julia_ml: Quick hypotheses: (a) streaming + batching may be merging partial arrays across inflight requests, producing truncated objects, and (b) a heuristic post-process could be injecting extra keys (e.g., `extra`) when model hallucinates metadata. Two mitigations to try:
- turn off streaming (stream:false) to confirm whether chunk-boundaries cause truncation.
- enable `json_mode.strict: true` (if available) or set `json_mode.coerce: false` to make the runtime fail early instead of patching output.

mike_eng: Also please try adding `sequence_id` per inference and set `stable_batching: true` in the request metadata; this forces the router to avoid interleaving responses from multiple concurrent requests on the same worker. If that stops the corruption, it's likely an ordering/merge bug in the streaming assembler.

acme_infra: Tried disabling stream and it succeeds (no parse error) — so streaming boundary looks related. Adding sequence_id + stable_batching as suggested also stopped the issue in our limited test.

julia_ml: Good repro, thanks. We'll promote a fix: guard the streaming assembler against concatenating partial JSON arrays from different requests and make the assembler emit a sentinel boundary per request. Eng-runtime will push a staging build in ~2h.

mike_eng: For now, recommended workarounds for production: 1) set stream:false; 2) include sequence_id and stable_batching:true; 3) tighten your client parser to accept partial chunks and only parse after final chunk or until a closing bracket `]` is seen. We'll follow up with a changelog entry.

eng-runtime-bot: Noted SUP-4821. Assigned to eng-runtime (mike_eng) and eng-ml (julia_ml). ETA staging build: 2 hours.

sarah_support: I'll follow up with the customer after staging release validation. acme_infra — can you please confirm whether you also saw extra keys (like `extra`) that are unexpected? Did those keys ever appear in non-streaming responses?

acme_infra: We only saw the hallucinated `extra` in streaming responses. Non-streaming responses matched the schema. Workaround applied for now. Thx team! :pray:

mike_eng: We'll post updates in this thread after staging validation and include the request ids from logs. Closing customer-facing loop when we've validated on prod.

sarah_support: Marking as customer-resolved for now pending eng confirmation. :white_check_mark:
